title: bun install: Content-Addressable Global Cache & Linux clonefile/reflink

progressiveExplaining.eli5: When npm installs packages, it downloads and unpacks thousands of duplicate files for every single project on your computer, filling up your disk and taking minutes. `bun install` downloads each package version once into a global vault. When your project needs it, it creates instant instant filesystem clones (`clonefile`/hardlinks) in milliseconds without copying bytes.
progressiveExplaining.junior: `bun install` is a drop-in replacement for `npm install` that is up to 25x faster. It uses a binary lockfile (`bun.lockb` or text `bun.lock` in Bun 1.2+) and a centralized global package cache located at `~/.bun/install/cache`. Instead of copying files, it uses the fastest available filesystem linking mechanism for your operating system.
progressiveExplaining.senior: Architecturally, `bun install` achieves speed via three vectors: (1) **Zig-native network pool**: HTTP requests, tarball decompression (using zlib/zstd), and package manifest parsing execute in parallel native threads. (2) **Content-addressable cache**: Tarball contents are unpacked into the global store once. (3) **Filesystem copy-on-write / Hardlinks**: On macOS (APFS), it uses `clonefile()` (instant copy-on-write pointer creation). On Linux, it uses `ioctl_ficlone` (reflink on Btrfs/XFS) or falls back to hardlinks, eliminating disk I/O.
progressiveExplaining.underTheHood: When resolving dependencies, Bun parses `package.json` with a custom SIMD-accelerated JSON parser. It queries the npm registry via a persistent HTTP/2 connection pool. Unpacking uses multi-threaded C bindings. When populating `node_modules`, Bun issues `clonefile(2)` syscalls from the cache directory directly to the project directory.

rosettaStone.npm: `npm install` (copies full files into `node_modules` per project).
rosettaStone.pnpm: `pnpm install` (uses global content-addressable store with symlinks).
rosettaStone.bun: `bun install` (uses global cache with native OS `clonefile` / `reflink` / hardlinks).

interviewGotchas.question: What is `bun.lockb` vs `bun.lock` in Bun?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Interviewers test your knowledge of Bun's lockfile format and Git diffing.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: `bun.lockb` is Bun's original **binary lockfile** format, designed for instant parsing without JSON deserialization overhead (saving ~100ms on startup). In Bun 1.2+, Bun introduced a human-readable text lockfile **`bun.lock`** (similar to yarn/pnpm) to make Git merge conflict resolution and code review diffs easy while retaining high install speeds.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: You can inspect a binary `bun.lockb` in the terminal at any time by running `bun bun.lockb` or `bun lockfile`.

interviewGotchas.question: Why is `bun install` faster than `pnpm` even though both use a global cache?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Checks understanding of native system implementation vs Node.js runtime overhead.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: While `pnpm` also uses a global store, it runs on Node.js and uses complex nested symlinks with JavaScript-level resolution. `bun install` is written entirely in compiled **Zig**, uses SIMD-accelerated JSON/lockfile parsing, executes concurrent network fetches in native C threads, and uses kernel-level Copy-on-Write (`clonefile`/`reflink`) directly.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Bun creates a standard flat `node_modules` structure by default, avoiding the symlink phantom-dependency traps that can occur with pnpm.
